sentences.text: Urbacodon is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur, a group of small carnivorous dinosaurs.
Currently, two species of this animal are known only from partial lower jaws.
Both specimens share a lightweight, strap-like lower jaw that curves inward at the tip, a symphyseal foramen, and thickened dentary teeth.
The holotype lower jaw of the first species is 79.2 mm long and contains 32 tooth positions.
Unlike most other troodontids, Urbacodon teeth lack serrations.
This dinosaur differs from Mei by being considerably larger and from Byronosaurus by having less vascularized lateral grooves and more bulbous front teeth.
The genus name Urbacodon is an acronym honoring scientists from Uzbekistan, Russia, Britain, America, and Canada.
A distinctive gap between the front and rear teeth exists in the holotype, though it may represent individual variation rather than a unique trait.
A lower jaw of Urbacodon was uncovered on September 9, 2004, near Itemir in Uzbekistan.
The type species Urbacodon itemirensis was named by Averianov and Sues in 2007.
The holotype of Urbacodon itemirensis is a single left lower jaw with replacement teeth from the Cenomanian Dzharakuduk Formation.
A second species, Urbacodon norelli, was described in 2024 based on a partial right lower jaw collected in the late 1990s.
A 2010 cladistic analysis identified Urbacodon as a close relative of Byronosaurus and Xixiasaurus.
Urbacodon lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 to 90 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Fossils are found in the Cenomanian Dzharakuduk Formation of Uzbekistan and the Iren Dabasu Formation of China.
Possible remains of Urbacodon are also known from the Turonian Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.
It is debated whether the distinctive gap between the front and rear teeth is a unique trait or merely individual variation.
